takeaways: Record equity highs driven by AI earnings are clashing with rising bond yields, as investors question the Fed's inflation commitment and the sustainability of massive AI capital expenditures.

Regulatory and environmental bottlenecks, including potential bans on Chinese components and power-use restrictions, threaten to inflate operational costs and delay the physical expansion of AI infrastructure.

Consumer sentiment is shifting toward hybrids over pure EVs, while global central banks face mounting pressure to balance cooling domestic demand against the long-term economic risks of climate change.

items.title: US stock market hits record highs as AI profits pile and oil prices ease
bullets: The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average reached record highs, driven by a 50% year-over-year growth in S&P 500 earnings per share, the largest increase since 2021.
Market sentiment was bolstered by a 5.3% decline in Brent crude prices to $79.36, reflecting reduced geopolitical risk regarding the Strait of Hormuz and easing inflationary concerns.
items.reason: Broad market rally to record highs driven by fundamental earnings growth.

items.title: SpaceX's first-ever earnings show a loss and huge spending
bullets: SpaceX reported a 92% revenue increase to $7.8 billion in its first public quarterly report, yet incurred a $2 billion net loss for the first half of the year due to massive capital expenditures.

The company allocated $18.3 billion to spending in the second quarter, primarily focused on scaling AI infrastructure, which has triggered investor concerns regarding the sustainability of its high-growth, high-burn model.
items.reason: Significant public debut earnings report for a major tech/AI player with high capital intensity.

items.title: ‘All hat, no cattle’: Markets question Fed’s inflation credibility amid elevated bond yields
bullets: The 30-year Treasury yield has reached its highest level since 2007, reflecting investor skepticism toward Chairman Warsh's commitment to a 2% inflation target following dovish-leaning press conference remarks.

Bank of America economists suggest the Fed must transition from rhetoric to action, projecting a 25 basis point hike in September followed by two additional increases in 2026 to restore market confidence.
items.reason: Direct impact on central bank policy expectations and long-term interest rate benchmarks.

items.title: Fitch Says: AI Market Correction Could Be a Big Risk to Corporate Credit. That Might Be Bad News for This Junk Bond ETF.
bullets: Fitch Ratings warns that AI-related capital expenditures, which contributed 1.4% to U.S. GDP growth in Q1 2026, create significant credit risks if the long-term profitability of these massive infrastructure investments fails to materialize.

With worldwide AI-related corporate debt issuance projected to hit $570 billion in 2026, a potential tech sector correction could disproportionately impact high-yield bond ETFs like JNK that hold debt from speculative or highly leveraged issuers.
items.reason: Highlights systemic credit risks tied to the current AI investment boom.

items.title: HSBC restarts buybacks as profits mushroom on Hong Kong growth
bullets: HSBC reported a 60% jump in second-quarter pre-tax profit to $10.1 billion, driven by higher net interest income and strong wealth management activity in the Hong Kong market.
The bank resumed share buybacks with a $1 billion program and raised its banking net interest income guidance to at least $46 billion, signaling confidence despite rising credit loss provisions.
items.reason: Major earnings beat and capital return announcement from a systemic financial institution.

items.title: Hong Kong Grade A office vacancy rate falls to 16.1% in Q2
bullets: The overall Grade A office vacancy rate dropped to 16.1% in Q2, with the Central and Admiralty districts seeing a significant 4.3 percentage point year-on-year decline in vacancy to 10.2%.

Colliers upgraded its rental growth forecast for core districts to 5-8% for the year, though decentralised areas like Kowloon East continue to face downward pressure with projected declines exceeding 5%.
items.reason: Key indicator of commercial real estate health and shifting demand patterns in the CBD.

items.title: Three major PC makers now using Chinese memory to fight 'unprecedented memory shortage,' report claims
bullets: HP, Asus, and Acer have begun integrating DRAM chips from Chinese manufacturer CXMT into select notebook models for non-U.S. markets to mitigate ongoing global memory supply constraints.
The move signals a potential shift in supply chain diversification, though it carries significant geopolitical risk as CXMT is currently under scrutiny by the Pentagon for alleged military ties.
items.reason: Supply chain diversification and geopolitical risk for major hardware OEMs.

items.title: ‘Apple is getting this wrong,’ says OpenAI — startup blasts iPhone maker over lawsuit alleging it stole confidential information through ex-Apple employees
bullets: OpenAI has formally challenged Apple’s lawsuit regarding alleged trade secret theft, asserting that the legal action is based on false information and is unnecessary for protecting Apple's intellectual property.

The litigation involves high-level personnel moves, including former Apple executives now at OpenAI, and threatens to disrupt OpenAI's strategic expansion into consumer hardware, specifically rumored AI-powered smart devices.
items.reason: Legal conflict between two major AI players impacting future hardware roadmaps.

items.title: 3 Magnificent Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks to Buy Right Now and Hold for the Next Decade
bullets: Cloud giants are reporting significant growth, with Amazon Web Services exceeding analyst expectations at 37% growth and Google Cloud posting an 82% revenue surge driven by AI chip sales.
Microsoft Azure maintains a strong 43% revenue growth rate, though investors should note that its growth trajectory has decelerated compared to the previous quarter's 40% year-over-year performance.
items.reason: Provides critical performance metrics for the primary AI infrastructure providers.

items.title: New York pauses some data center proposals as scrutiny grows over AI power and water use
bullets: Regulatory pushback in New York regarding data center power and water consumption signals a potential bottleneck for the physical expansion of AI infrastructure.
Investors should monitor this trend as increased environmental oversight could lead to higher operational costs and delayed project timelines for hyperscalers and data center REITs.
items.reason: Highlights a growing regulatory risk factor impacting AI infrastructure scalability.

items.title: SpaceX to Build AI Infrastructure Exclusively on Nvidia Systems
bullets: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk announced that the company will exclusively utilize Nvidia's Vera Rubin architecture for its AI computing needs, targeting a massive scale of 10 gigawatts of capacity by the end of next year.

The partnership includes plans to deploy Nvidia's NVL72 rackscale systems both on the ground and in space, as SpaceX leverages its public status to monetize data center capacity through leasing agreements with firms like Google and Anthropic.
items.reason: Major enterprise commitment to Nvidia's next-gen architecture.

items.title: MediaTek Targets 20% of Custom AI Chip Market, Challenging Broadcom
bullets: MediaTek has raised its 2027 market share target to 15-20% of the $80 billion custom AI-chip sector, with its first AI accelerator for a major U.S. cloud provider entering production in Q4 2026.

While Broadcom remains deeply embedded in Google's roadmap through 2031, MediaTek's entry as a potential second ASIC partner offers Alphabet increased leverage over supply chain costs and design capacity.
items.reason: Significant competitive shift in the custom AI silicon supply chain.

items.title: EVs Slump, Hybrids Soar: Hyundai and Kia Reports Best July Sales
bullets: Hyundai and Kia reported record-breaking July sales of 165,284 units, driven by a 52.2% surge in hybrid vehicle demand that offset significant declines in pure electric vehicle performance.

Pure EV sales for the brands cratered, with the Ioniq 6 dropping 92% and the Electrified GV70 falling 96%, signaling a sharp consumer pivot toward hybrids amid persistent interest rate pressures and cooling EV sentiment.
items.reason: Highlights a major shift in consumer preference from BEVs to hybrids for major automakers.

items.title: Volvo EV Sales Jump 33% in July as the Brand Readies a Cheaper EX50 for 2027
bullets: Volvo achieved its strongest year-over-year growth of 2026 with a 33.2% increase in fully electric vehicle deliveries in July, even as total company sales declined 4% due to a downturn in the Chinese market.

The company is successfully transitioning its portfolio toward battery-electric models, with BEV deliveries rising 21% over the last three months while plug-in hybrid sales experienced a 10.9% decline in July.
items.reason: Demonstrates successful EV portfolio transition despite broader regional headwinds.

items.title: Trump Plans Ban On Chinese Data Center Components
bullets: The administration is drafting rules to ban the import of Chinese optical receivers, critical components for data transmission, citing risks of digital espionage and intellectual property theft.

This potential restriction could force major U.S. hyperscalers like Amazon, Microsoft, and Meta to pivot to higher-cost domestic suppliers, further inflating capital expenditure projections for AI infrastructure.
items.reason: Direct impact on supply chain costs and geopolitical risk for major tech firms.

items.title: Rate of play: How US states are changing the rules around data centers and power
bullets: Over 300 pieces of legislation have been filed at state and federal levels in 2026, as regulators struggle to manage the unprecedented energy demand from AI-driven data center clusters.

Legislative efforts include proposed moratoriums and new rate classes, signaling a shift away from the traditional utility model and creating significant uncertainty for long-term infrastructure investment and operational costs.
items.reason: Regulatory headwinds threaten the scalability and cost-efficiency of future data center projects.

items.title: SpaceX reports 92% revenue jump in first post-IPO earnings
bullets: SpaceX reported a 92% year-over-year revenue increase in its inaugural quarterly earnings release as a public company, driven primarily by robust growth in Starlink subscriptions and rising demand for AI compute infrastructure.

The company has formally organized its operations into three distinct business segments—space, connectivity, and AI—and confirmed a strategic commitment to exclusively utilize Nvidia hardware for its expanding data center footprint.
items.reason: Market-moving financial disclosure for a newly public major aerospace entity.

items.title: US Space Force Awards SpaceX $1.6 Billion for Falcon 9 Launches
bullets: The U.S. Space Force has awarded SpaceX a $1.6 billion contract for Falcon 9 launch services, underscoring the company's critical role in national security space operations and its dominance in the launch market.

This contract award coincides with reports that SpaceX's launch manifest is effectively booked through 2029, creating significant barriers to entry for competitors reliant on the company's launch infrastructure.
items.reason: Significant government contract reinforcing long-term revenue visibility and market dominance.
